caption: The day view
preconditions: Newsroom seed from tools/screenshots/SEED.md has run (users marenholt, tomasvidal, priyaraman, danielokafor, elinesund, lucabrandt exist and are active)

Availability data seeded by seed.py (SEED.md, AVAILABILITY_TAGS, AVAILABILITY, AVAILABILITY_OVERRIDES): vocabulary 'availability_manager_tags' ('Regions': North Aldmark with Arlenport and Kestrel Bay, South Aldmark with Saltmere, Eastbrook and Vennhaven), default weeks for the six seeded users and admin with available, partial and unavailable days, and tomasvidal's entry for tomorrow set to unavailable by admin
Today is a weekday (Mon-Fri) so the rows show a mix of Available all day, partial hours and Unavailable
steps: Open #/availability-management and wait for [data-test-id="day-view"] to be visible
Make sure the 'Day' option in [data-test-id="filter-type"] is selected (it is the default)
Wait until [data-test-id="day-view"] shows 'Maren Holt'
notes: Replaces .gitbook/assets/availability_dailyview.png, which was taken on a customer staging server and shows the customer's name and real people. Rows are coloured by status (success/warning/alert). Filters in the header: Languages, Status, Regions (the vocabulary display name). Do not use the e2e 'availability-management' snapshot: its users are named after TV characters and its dates are in 1970 (the e2e specs fix the clock to 1970-02-03).

caption: An availability manager edits another user's availability
preconditions: Newsroom seed from tools/screenshots/SEED.md has run (users marenholt, tomasvidal, priyaraman, danielokafor, elinesund, lucabrandt exist and are active)

Availability data seeded by seed.py (SEED.md, AVAILABILITY_TAGS, AVAILABILITY, AVAILABILITY_OVERRIDES): vocabulary 'availability_manager_tags' ('Regions': North Aldmark with Arlenport and Kestrel Bay, South Aldmark with Saltmere, Eastbrook and Vennhaven), default weeks for the six seeded users and admin with available, partial and unavailable days, and tomasvidal's entry for tomorrow set to unavailable by admin
Admin has the user_availability and user_availability_manage privileges (administrators have all privileges)
steps: Open #/availability-management and wait for [data-test-id="day-view"] to be visible
Wait for [data-test-id="working-day-view"] to be visible
Wait for [data-test-id="edit-workday"] to be visible
notes: Replaces .gitbook/assets/grafik (13).png (customer instance, real names). Clicking the user's name or avatar opens a modal titled with the user's display name that contains their full availability settings; clicking a day with an entry opens the summary (Edit, Remove, Close icon buttons), Edit opens the 'Edit availability' modal with Available / Unavailable / Partially available and the Regions field. The IconButton's accessible name is 'Edit'; if button[aria-label="Edit"] does not match, use role=button:Edit inside working-day-view. Leave the modal without saving; nothing to clean up. Capture: the user's modal has no [data-test-id=availability-settings] (that id is only on the profile page); the steps wait for the day buttons in [role=dialog] and open tomorrow, the first 'unavailable' day, which the seed set for tomasvidal (Modified by admin).

caption: Manage the availability tasks and subtasks
preconditions: Availability data seeded by seed.py (SEED.md, AVAILABILITY_TAGS, AVAILABILITY, AVAILABILITY_OVERRIDES): vocabulary 'availability_manager_tags' ('Regions': North Aldmark with Arlenport and Kestrel Bay, South Aldmark with Saltmere, Eastbrook and Vennhaven), default weeks for the six seeded users and admin with available, partial and unavailable days, and tomasvidal's entry for tomorrow set to unavailable by admin
steps: Open #/settings/vocabularies and wait for [data-test-id="metadata-content"] to be visible
Hover [data-test-id="vocabulary-item"] with text 'Regions'
Wait for the vocabulary edit modal 'Edit Regions' to be visible
Click 'Items' in the modal's left navigation
notes: Replaces .gitbook/assets/grafik (14).png, which shows a customer's vocabulary names in the background. Full frame so the Settings > Metadata page shows behind the modal. Close the modal with Cancel afterwards; do not save. The items are the towns (Arlenport, Eastbrook, ...) with their region as parent; 'North Aldmark' is not an item label. The item names are input values, so there is no text to wait for; the step waits for the network to settle.
